source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Brian watched 141 stock videos across 21 channels, tallied the five most-covered companies, and gives his own verdict plus entry-price ladder for each. Alphabet/Google (BUY @ ~$362) split creators three ways: Nolan and Parkev are bullish (Parkev sees $410-450 by end of 2027), while Daniel Pronk passes at fair value $354 as the most expensive hyperscaler, and Steve Eisman sold to reduce AI exposure ('it's all one trade'). Brian leans positive long-term on DCA, noting Google looks cheap on earnings but rich on sales. Nvidia (BUY): Parkev sees fair value $300 vs ~$221, but Felix warns Nvidia's CDS costs doubled in three months, with pension funds financing ~$500B of chips that could be obsolete in five years; Brian's fair value is ~$290. Micron (BUY): liked for capacity sold out through 2027, but a cheap multiple at record earnings can mark a cycle top; his model says fair value ~$1,450 yet he takes a smaller bite since history says it's richly valued, with a $434 exit line if the story breaks. CoreWeave (no call): he gives no ladder at all — 17 months of public history is too little to price, despite Parkev's $113 fair value. Uber (BUY): Parkev's $120 vs his own $109 — near-identical independent valuations — deepest buy band, with driverless cars the key break-risk. His broader thesis: 76 of 141 videos covered chips, clouds, or models — most YouTuber watch lists are 'one bet wearing five different names.'
title: 21 YouTubers Agree on 5 Stocks. My Entry Points
